name: github
summary: GitHub's own hosted MCP server: repos, issues, pull requests, Actions (personal access token)
notes: Endpoint https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/ is GitHub's own remote MCP server; GitHub says it is available to every GitHub user, and a tool behind a paid feature (Copilot cloud agent) needs that plan.

Credential: a personal access token sent as Authorization: Bearer. A fine-grained token limited to the repositories you want is best. Put it in the store yourself, in your own terminal: lotr secret put github-pat.
Read-only instead: use https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/readonly as the url (a copy of this template under your own name); GitHub then offers only read tools.

GitHub's browser sign-in for this server needs an OAuth app you create and does not register clients itself, so this template uses the token; a sign-in variant would be the mcp-oauth-preregistered archetype.

Tiers: names with a risky word (create, update, merge, delete, write, commit...) are consent on their own; the policy pins merges, file pushes and every *_write tool as consent, keeps comments a write, and makes the reads whose names do not show it reads: issue_read, pull_request_read, the Actions and Projects getters, and the commit readers (get_commit, list_commits, search_commits, which hold the risky word 'commit').
This is an alternative to the built-in REST connection (lotr add-http ... --profile github), which keeps working.
